new.s: Which of the following was NOT a part of the 1991 New Economic Policy?
o: Automatic approval for FDI in priority industries
Expansion of the list of industries reserved for the public sector
new.x: The 1991 policy cut licensing and shrank the public-sector reserved list; it never expanded State control.
new.angle: U0367 #3 / PYQ y988820cc4e1 not a feature of NEP

new.s:
Consider the following statements about rupee convertibility:
1. The rupee was made convertible on the current account in 1994.
2. Full capital account convertibility was adopted as part of the 1991 LPG reforms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Current account convertibility came in 1994; capital account convertibility was never fully adopted and was not part of LPG.
new.angle: U0367 #3 / PYQ y576b449dca6 measure not part of LPG

new.s: On which date was the New Economic Policy (LPG) announced in India?
new.x: The NEP was announced on 24 July 1991 by PM P.V. Narasimha Rao's government with FM Manmohan Singh.

new.s: What was the trigger of India's 1991 balance of payments crisis?
new.x: NRI deposits flowed out, and forex reserves fell to about $975 million, enough for about two weeks of imports.

new.s: Which of the following committees dealt with insurance sector reform?
new.x: The Malhotra Committee (1993) dealt with insurance; Narasimham covered banking and Chelliah tax.

new.s: With which sector was the Narasimham Committee (1991) concerned?
new.x: The Narasimham Committee (1991, second in 1998) recommended banking sector reforms.

new.s: In which year did India move to a market-determined exchange rate?
new.x: After the 1991 devaluation, India moved to a market-determined exchange rate in 1993.

new.s: Which sector does the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB), set up in 2006, regulate?
new.x: PNGRB (2006) regulates petroleum products and gas pipelines; TRAI handles telecom and CERC power.

new.s: In which year were the last items reserved for the small-scale sector de-reserved?
new.x: The last SSI-reserved items were de-reserved in 2015; defence was opened to private players in 2001.

new.s: Who are the authors of 'Reinventing Government' (1992)?
new.x: David Osborne and Ted Gaebler wrote Reinventing Government (1992), with the idea 'steering, not rowing'.

new.s: Which principle of Reinventing Government means 'earn rather than spend'?
new.x: Enterprising government earns rather than spends; catalytic government steers rather than rows.

new.s: What was India's rank in the UN E-Government Development Index (EGDI) 2024?
new.x: India was ranked 97th in the UN EGDI 2024.

new.s: To what age has Andhra Pradesh raised the upper age limit for non-uniform direct recruitment, till 30 September 2027?
new.x: G.O. Ms. No. 187 raised the limit from 42 to 44 years till 30 September 2027.
new.angle: U0369 #5 notes gap: AP age limit

new.s: How many indicators does GRAI use to rank central ministries on CPGRAMS grievance disposal?
new.x: GRAI uses 11 indicators grouped into 4 dimensions.

new.s: Which body is regarded as a symbol of competitive federalism, having replaced the Planning Commission's allocation role?
new.x: NITI Aayog symbolises competitive federalism; the GST Council symbolises cooperative federalism.

new.s: For which States are core Centrally Sponsored Schemes funded in the Centre:State ratio of 90:10?
o: States with a fiscal deficit above 3% of GSDP
new.x: Core CSS are mostly 60:40, but 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

new.s: Who chaired the 14th Finance Commission?
new.x: Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th FC (2015-20), which raised the States' share from 32% to 42%.

new.s: How many sectors are covered under the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0?
new.x: NMP 2.0 (FY26-FY30) covers 12 sectors, led by highways at 26%.

new.s: Since which year has the Offer for Sale (OFS) route been used for disinvestment?
new.x: The OFS method of selling shares of listed PSEs has been used since 2012.

new.s: Under which PPP model is Bhogapuram airport in Andhra Pradesh being developed by GMR?
new.x: Bhogapuram airport is a DBFOT project with GMR on a 40-year concession.

new.s: Under the Hybrid Annuity Model, over about how many years is the developer's 60% share repaid through semi-annual annuities?
new.x: In HAM the government pays 40% during construction and repays the developer's 60% through annuities over about 15 years.
new.angle: U0371 #2 notes gap: HAM annuity period

new.s: What does the Finance Commission constituted under Article 280 recommend?
o: Allocation of Plan funds to Union Ministries
Rates of GST on goods and services
Distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States
Borrowing limits of the States under Article 293
new.x: The Finance Commission recommends how the net proceeds of taxes are shared between the Union and the States.
new.angle: U0372 PYQ y6dfb7889bf8 tax sharing -> Finance Commission

new.s: Which of the following is an advisory body that studies law reform and submits its reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice?
new.x: The Law Commission is an advisory research body set up by executive notification; it reports to the Law Ministry.
new.angle: U0372 N1 / PYQ yc3d547305e9 Law Commission -> function

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Law Commission of India:
1. It is constituted by an executive notification for a term of three years.
2. It is a quasi-judicial body.
3. It submits its reports to the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Law Commission is set up by notification every three years; it is advisory, not quasi-judicial, and reports to the Law Ministry.
new.angle: U0372 N1 Law Commission status / PYQ y770146971b5

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Election Commission of India?
new.x: Article 324 provides for the Election Commission; 315 is for PSCs and 280 for the Finance Commission.

new.s: How many members, including the Chairman, does the Finance Commission have?
new.x: The Finance Commission has five members: a Chairman and four others.

new.s: Who was the first Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission?
new.x: Justice Ranganath Misra was the first Chairman of the NHRC, set up in 1993.
new.angle: U0372 #5 notes gap: NHRC first chair

new.s: Who was the first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog?
new.x: Arvind Panagariya was NITI Aayog's first Vice-Chairman; Gulzarilal Nanda was the Planning Commission's first.
new.angle: U0372 #5 notes gap: NITI first VC

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a statutory body?
new.x: The CBI is non-statutory; it draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946. CVC, NCW and NGT have their own Acts.

new.s: Who among the following select the Director of the CBI?
o: President, Prime Minister and Home Minister
Prime Minister, Home Minister and Central Vigilance Commissioner
Chief Justice of India, Speaker and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India (or nominee) and Leader of the Opposition
new.x: A committee of the PM, the CJI or a nominated judge, and the Leader of the Opposition selects the CBI Director.
new.angle: U0372 #3 notes gap: CBI Director selection

new.s: In which year was the Planning Commission set up by a Government resolution?
new.x: The Planning Commission was set up by a resolution of 15 March 1950; the NDC followed in 1952.
new.angle: U0372 #5 notes gap: Planning Commission year

new.s: Under which Article of the Constitution is the report of the Finance Commission laid before Parliament?
new.x: Under Article 281 the President lays the FC report before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum.
new.angle: U0372 #9 notes gap: FC report Article

new.s: On whose recommendation was the Inter-State Council set up in 1990?
new.x: The President set up the Inter-State Council under Article 263 in 1990 on the advice of the Sarkaria Commission.
